question: A force that changes the state of motion of an object is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Unbalanced force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Unbalanced force** is a force that causes a change in the state of motion of an object. It is responsible for accelerating or decelerating an object, changing its direction, or altering its shape.
 
• An unbalanced force occurs when the net force acting on an object is not equal to zero. This results in a change in the object's velocity, which could mean a change in speed, direction, or both.
 
• For example, when a person pushes a stationary object with enough force to overcome friction and inertia, the object moves. This motion occurs due to the unbalanced force acting on it.
 
• In the absence of unbalanced forces, an object will either remain stationary (if initially at rest) or continue moving in a straight line at constant speed (if initially in motion). This is in accordance with **Newton's First Law of Motion**.
 
• Unbalanced forces are fundamental to many phenomena in daily life, such as driving a car, playing sports, or the movement of celestial bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Balanced Force:**

 
 
• When the net force acting on an object is zero, the forces are termed as balanced forces.
 
• Balanced forces do not change the state of motion of an object; they keep it at rest or moving uniformly in a straight line.
 
• Example: A book resting on a table experiences balanced forces – the force of gravity pulling it down is balanced by the upward normal force exerted by the table.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Force:**
 
 
• This is the attractive force exerted by a massive body, such as Earth, on other objects.
 
• It is responsible for phenomena like objects falling to the ground and the orbits of planets around the Sun.
 
• Gravitational force acts on all objects with mass and is proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
 
 
• **Frictional Force:**
 
 
• Friction is a force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact.
 
• It acts parallel to the surfaces and can either prevent motion (static friction) or resist motion (kinetic friction).
 
• Frictional force plays a crucial role in enabling walking, driving, and holding objects but also causes wear and heat generation.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:**
 
 
• Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia): An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
 
• Newton's Second Law: The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass (F = ma).
 
• Newton's Third Law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Unbalanced Forces:**
 
 
• Unbalanced forces are responsible for starting, stopping, and changing the direction of motion in vehicles.
 
• They are crucial in sports, where players apply forces to accelerate, decelerate, or change the direction of balls or themselves.
 
• Rocket launches utilize unbalanced forces generated by the expulsion of gases to propel themselves upward.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Force:**

 
 
• Force is defined as a push or pull that can cause an object to accelerate, decelerate, or change its shape or direction.
 
• It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• The SI unit of force is the **Newton (N)**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Unbalanced Forces:**
 
 
• A car accelerating on a highway experiences unbalanced forces due to the engine's thrust overcoming air resistance and friction.
 
• When a ball is kicked, the force applied by the foot overcomes the balanced forces of gravity and friction, causing motion.
 
• A spacecraft maneuvering in outer space applies unbalanced forces via thrusters to change its velocity or direction.
 
 
 
• **Practical Implications:**
 
 
• Understanding unbalanced forces helps in designing efficient vehicles, aircraft, and machinery.
 
• It aids in predicting and controlling the motion of objects in sports and engineering applications.
